intro: The formal letter and email: how to open, state your purpose, ask, and close.
p.dirigirse a.consejo: With yo the g becomes j: «me dirijo». It is the formal way to start a letter.
p.estimado.consejo: It opens a letter: «estimado señor», «estimada señora». It changes gender with the person.
p.en relación con.consejo: It is written as three words, without «a»: «en relación con su anuncio». It is formal.
p.ponerse en contacto con.consejo: It is pronominal: «me pongo en contacto con ustedes». It is very common in letters and emails.
p.adjuntar.consejo: You say «le adjunto mi currículum». An email carries «archivos adjuntos».
p.solicitud.consejo: It is feminine and ends in -ud: «la solicitud». The stress goes at the end: so-li-thi-TUD.
p.quedar a su disposición.consejo: It is a closing formula. It is said in the first person: «quedo a su disposición».
p.a la espera de sus noticias.glosa: looking forward to hearing from you
p.a la espera de sus noticias.consejo: It is a formula before the closing. Here «noticias» means «reply or information».
p.sin otro particular.consejo: It is an old closing formula. It is used less today: «sin otro particular, le saluda atentamente».
p.atentamente.consejo: It comes from «atento» plus «-mente». It goes at the end, followed by a comma and your name.
p.un cordial saludo.consejo: It is the most used closing in emails today. It takes a comma at the end: «un cordial saludo,».
p.remitente.consejo: It works for men and women: «el remitente», «la remitente». It goes on the back of the envelope.
p.destinatario.consejo: It is the opposite of «remitente». Its name goes on the front of the envelope.
p.asunto.consejo: In an email it should say clearly what you want. It is masculine: «el asunto».
b1.titulo: The skeleton of a formal letter
b1.texto:
**1. Greeting.** Always followed by a colon, not a comma:

- **Estimado señor García:**
- **Estimados señores:** (when you do not know who will read it)

**2. Purpose.**

- **Me dirijo a usted para** solicitar información.
- **Le escribo en relación con** su anuncio.
- **Me pongo en contacto con ustedes**…

**3. Body.** Use **usted**, the conditional and the imperfect subjunctive:

- **Le agradecería que** me **enviara**…
- **Quisiera saber si**…
- **Le adjunto** mi currículum.

**4. Before closing.**

- **Quedo a su disposición** para cualquier aclaración.
- **A la espera de sus noticias**, le saluda atentamente,

**5. Closing.** With a comma and your name on the next line: **Atentamente,** / **Un cordial saludo,**

In an email, **el asunto** must say clearly what you want. On an envelope, **el destinatario** goes on the front and **el remitente** on the back.
b2.f0.texto: How do you start the letter?
b2.f3.texto: I am writing to you in connection with the research grants.
b2.f4.texto: And what do you want to ask?
b2.f5.texto: I would like to know whether it is possible to submit the application by email.
b2.f7.texto: I would be grateful if you could tell me the necessary documents.
b2.f9.texto: I attach my CV and remain at your disposal.
b4.titulo: The five parts of a letter
b4.texto:
A formal letter has five parts:

- **Greeting**, with a colon: **Estimado señor García:**
- **Purpose**: **me dirijo a usted para** + infinitive; **en relación con** + noun.
- **Body**: **le agradecería que** + imperfect subjunctive; **quisiera saber si** + indicative.
- **Close**: **quedo a su disposición**; **a la espera de sus noticias**.
- **Sign-off**, with a comma: **atentamente,** / **un cordial saludo,**

In an email, **el asunto** sums up the purpose in a few words.
b4.e0.texto: I am writing to you to request information.
b4.e1.texto: I attach a copy of the invoice.
b4.e2.texto: I remain at your disposal for any clarification.
b5.f0.texto: Nerea writes the first line by hand in small, firm handwriting.
b5.f1.texto: The pen scratches the white paper with a soft sound.
b5.f2.texto: Next to the lamp, an empty envelope waits with the address already written.
b5.f3.texto: The addressee appears at the top, with his name in capital letters.
b5.f4.texto: Nerea reads the sentence quietly and swaps one word for a more polite one.
b5.f5.texto: Outside, the wind moves the leaves of the garden with a long whisper.
b5.f6.texto: Nerea folds the letter into three equal parts and puts it in the envelope.
b5.f7.texto: On the back she writes her name as sender in small letters.
b5.f8.texto: She runs her tongue along the edge of the envelope and feels a soft taste of paper.
b5.f9.texto: The envelope stays on the table, white and silent, awaiting your news.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «Estimado señor García:» takes a colon.
b6.o1.refuerzo: The comma goes after the sign-off, not after the greeting.
b6.o2.refuerzo: An exclamation mark is too informal.
b6.pregunta: Which mark follows the greeting in a formal letter?
b7.frase: Le agradecería que me ____ el formulario.
b7.o1.refuerzo: It is indicative; after «que» here comes the subjunctive.
b7.o2.refuerzo: The future does not work after «que» in a request.
b8.frase: Quedo a su disposición para cualquier aclaración
b8.traduccion: I remain at your disposal for any clarification
b9.o0.refuerzo: It is a sign-off for family or friends.
b9.o1.refuerzo: It is a spoken, informal goodbye.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Yes: it is a formal and kind sign-off.
b10.frase: Me ____ a usted para pedir información.
b10.o0.refuerzo: With yo, the g becomes j: «dirigo» does not exist.
b10.o1.refuerzo: Yes: «dirigir» changes g to j before o.
b10.o2.refuerzo: It is the form for «él» or «usted», not «yo».
b10.pregunta: Choose the right form of the verb.
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «I attach my CV.»
b12.o0.refuerzo: The person who writes it is the sender.
b12.o1.refuerzo: Yes: the addressee is whoever receives the letter.
b12.o2.refuerzo: The person who delivers it is the postman, not the addressee.
b12.pregunta: Who is the addressee of a letter?
p.empiezas.consejo: «empezar» changes e to ie. The c before e sounds like th.
p.becas.consejo: Money given to help study or research. The v sounds like b.
p.posible.consejo: Its opposite is «imposible». The v sounds like b.
p.petición.consejo: From «pedir», to ask. The accent shows the stress on ón.
p.indicara.consejo: Imperfect subjunctive after «que», in polite requests.
p.documentos.consejo: Papers with official information. Plural of «documento».
p.cortesía.consejo: From «cortés», polite. Use it for good manners.
p.quedo.consejo: In letters, «quedo a su disposición» means I remain at your service.
p.disposición.consejo: «a su disposición» means available to you.
p.copia.consejo: A duplicate of a document. The c before o sounds like k.
p.araña.consejo: «arañar» means to scratch lightly. The ñ sounds like ny.
p.vacío.consejo: Its opposite is «lleno», full. The v sounds like b.
p.escrita.consejo: Participle of «escribir» in feminine form for «dirección».
p.cortés.consejo: Its noun form is «cortesía». The accent marks the stress.
p.susurro.consejo: A soft sound, like the wind. From «susurrar».
p.atrás.consejo: «en la parte de atrás» means on the back side.
p.lengua.consejo: Also means language. The g before u sounds like g.
p.sabor.consejo: From «saber», to know. The v-like b: «sabor» has no v sound.
